title: SERP API Pricing: Plans and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: SerpApi pricing includes monthly plans with search allowances and throughput limits; compare costs across tiers to find your match.
body_markdown:
## Cost per 1,000 searches at realistic monthly volumes


$25.00 per 1,000 searches on the smallest plan, $5.50 on the largest: that is the range at full quota, so customers on the smallest tier effectively pay nearly 5 times more per search.


The same search costs more than four times as much depending on where you sit on the ladder.


### Per-1,000 cost across the plan ladder


Divide each plan's monthly price by its search quota, both taken from[SerpApi's pricing page](https://serpapi.com/pricing) , and you get the figures below. The arithmetic is ours, not a vendor claim.


Starter works out to $25.00 per 1,000, so a team that picks it for the low card price pays the most for every search.


Per SerpApi, Developer comes to $15.00, and Production to $10.00 ($150 for 15,000 searches), which means production deployments are more cost-effective. Per SerpApi, Big Data is $9.17, Searcher $7.25 and Infrastructure $5.50, making infrastructure the most affordable option.


Moving from Starter to Production cuts the unit cost by $15.00, while moving from Big Data to Infrastructure cuts it by only $3.67, so early-stage upgrades deliver substantially more cost savings.


Every figure assumes you use the whole quota. **A plan that sits half empty costs twice what the chart says.**


### Three usage profiles and the plan each lands on


Check 500 keywords daily and you run 500 × 30 = 15,000 searches, which is exactly the Production quota. That's $10.00 per 1,000 with no headroom, so one rerun of failed checks goes straight to overage.


Treat Production as the minimum and check the next tier up before committing.


You can't place a 20-client agency from client count alone. Multiply each client's keywords by check frequency, add them up, and add the ad-hoc searches your account managers run when a client emails asking why a ranking dropped.


Hardest to place is the AI agent with unpredictable lookups. Size it to a typical busy month, not an average one. Too small means overage on the worst days, and too large means paying for quota nobody calls.


### Where upgrading costs more than overage


For a one-off spike, such as a client audit or a backfill, absorbing it as overage is usually cheaper than fixing it by moving up a tier. The upgrade charges a full month for quota you won't use again.


When a spike repeats every month, the case is the opposite. Compare the overage rate on the pricing page with the next tier's per-1,000 figure from the ladder above. If overage is higher, the upgrade is the cheaper way to cover the extra searches.
